title: AI Design Suite — per-project component capabilities manifest
description: Schema for a consuming project's own component-capabilities file (conventionally .design-suite/component-capabilities.json, pointed to by profile.json's componentCapabilities.file). Same two-source split as component-maturity.schema.json, for the same reason: some facts about a component ARE mechanically recoverable and some are not, and conflating the two is how a file drifts from reality without anyone noticing. Per component, two layers: `derived` (machine-written, never hand-edited — regenerated the way docs/CATALOG.md is regenerated from frontmatter, by the same constructor-shape extraction audit_promotion_candidates.py already runs) and `capabilities` (hand-authored, optional, `additionalProperties: false` throughout so nobody invents new vocabulary per-project rather than proposing it here). Constructor shape (prop names/types) is exactly what a script already knows from parsing the widget; accessibility behaviour and which states a component actually handles are not recoverable from a signature alone (a `loading` bool parameter does not prove a spinner renders) and need a human to say so, the same reasoning `component-maturity.schema.json`'s free-text notes/evidence fields use. An entry — or a field within `capabilities` — absent entirely must read as 'unknown', never as 'has none': this is also why every capabilities sub-object is optional rather than defaulted to false/empty, and why consumers (audit_reinvented_components.py, audit_promotion_candidates.py) that gate on capability overlap must treat a missing capabilities block as 'nothing to compare', not as 'no overlap'. Designed with issue #58's eventual query needs in mind (a tool matching a natural-language UI need against components needs exactly `capabilities.states`/`a11y`/`variants` to query over) without building that tool here.

prop.description: One constructor parameter, as extracted mechanically. Deliberately thin — this is what a signature can prove, nothing more.

type.description: Declared type as written in source, free text (e.g. `String`, `VoidCallback?`). Absent when the extractor could not isolate a type, which happens for `this.foo`-style shorthand params — absence here is 'not recovered', not 'untyped'.

required.description: Whether the parameter is required at the call site. Absent means the extractor could not determine this, not that it is optional.

derived.description: Machine-generated. Never hand-edit this block — regenerate it instead, the same rule CLAUDE.md states for docs/CATALOG.md. A tool that regenerates this file overwrites `derived` wholesale per component and leaves `capabilities` untouched.

props.description: Constructor parameter shape, from the same extraction audit_promotion_candidates.py's constructor_params() already performs. Order is not meaningful; this is a set of props, not a call signature.

framework.description: e.g. `flutter`, `react`, `swiftui` — from the adapter that found this component, i.e. profile.json's adapters.lang or an adapter-specific label. Free text because the suite's adapters are not a closed set.

platform.description: Runtime/platform this shape was extracted for, when it differs from framework (e.g. a Flutter web-only widget). Free text; omit when framework already says everything worth saying.

sourcePath.description: Repo-relative path to the file the shape was extracted from.

generatedAt.description: Free text: a date, a commit SHA, a run identifier — whatever the regenerating tool wants to stamp so staleness is at least visible, never enforced by this schema.

a11y.description: Accessibility facts, hand-verified. Each is a boolean because these are true/false facts about the built component (does it respond to keyboard focus, does it read out a label, does focus render visibly), not a judgement call like `component-maturity`'s status. Any field absent means 'not verified either way', never 'false' — an audit reading this must treat a missing key as unknown, the same rule the file-level description states for a whole missing entry.

keyboardNav.description: Reachable and operable via keyboard alone (tab order, enter/space activation, arrow-key navigation where applicable).

screenReaderLabel.description: Exposes a semantic label/role a screen reader announces — not just visible text.

focusVisible.description: Renders a visible focus indicator when focused via keyboard.

capabilities.description: Hand-authored, optional. Absent means unknown, not 'no capabilities' — see the file-level description. `additionalProperties: false` so a project proposes new vocabulary here rather than inventing an undocumented field a consumer can't read.

states.description: Which of the standard interaction states this component actually handles (renders a distinct visual/behaviour for), verified by a human — not inferred from a boolean constructor param, which does not prove the state is implemented.

variants.description: Free-text visual/behavioural variants this component supports (size, emphasis, color scheme, ...). Free text deliberately: a component's variant set (a DsButton's sizes, a chat bubble's alignment) cannot be enumerated generically the way `states` can.

notes.description: Free-text context a boolean/array can't carry — same role as component-maturity's `notes` field.

components.description: Keyed the same way component-maturity.schema.json's `components` map is keyed — however the project names its own components, used consistently, because that key is the join point other tooling (the duplicate-detection audits, a future #58 query engine) looks up by.

_readme: CANONICAL. Schema for a per-project component-capabilities file — see issue #61 and docs/ROADMAP.md master backlog (issue #38) item 18. profile.json's optional componentCapabilities.file field points at the populated instance; nothing in the universal plugin hardcodes its path or its project's component names. `derived` is regenerated by tooling (design_suite/engine/component_shape.py's derive helper, called from audit_promotion_candidates.py and available to any regenerating script); `capabilities` is hand-maintained and untouched by tooling. Sequenced to land before issue #58 (a 'which component should I use' query tool) so #58 queries a schema that was designed for querying, not one bent to fit it after the fact.
